transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, so… I came in because things at work have gotten really hard to just ignore. I’m a transportation inspector, and ever since I got that county safety award, there’s been this shift. Certain people at work have been taking my inspection reports and, I don’t know, twisting them—making it seem like I wrote things a different way than I did, or like I missed something on purpose.

And then there are these budget questions they keep asking, but they’re not normal questions. They’re pointed, like they’re trying to connect me to something improper, like I’m crooked or taking shortcuts. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, routine stuff, but I know how normal review feels. This doesn’t feel like that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me because of the attention I got from that award. I’m not trying to sound dramatic, but I can tell when people are lining things up against me.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially since these issues at work started?

I don’t know if I’d call it “down” exactly. I mean, I’m frustrated, definitely, and I’ve been preoccupied with what’s happening at work because it’s hard not to be when people are picking apart your reports and acting like you did something wrong. But hopeless? No, I wouldn’t say that.

As far as losing interest, I guess I’ve been more distracted than anything. Like if I’m doing something I normally enjoy, my mind can drift back to work and I start thinking through who said what or why they asked a certain question. But it’s not like I suddenly don’t care about things anymore. It’s more that this situation keeps taking up space in my head.
Have you ever felt like people at work are not just criticizing you but actually plotting against you in ways that others might not understand or believe?

Yes. That’s… honestly, that’s why I’m here. It’s not just “criticism” in the normal workplace sense, like somebody saying a report needs a correction or asking me to clarify something. I can handle that. I’ve been doing inspections long enough to know there’s always review and paperwork and people double-checking things.

But this feels different. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people started acting differently around me, and then my inspection reports started getting picked apart in ways that don’t seem random. Like they’ll focus on a phrase I used and make it sound like I meant something else, or they’ll ask about something as if I was trying to hide it. And the budget questions—those are the part that really bother me—because they’re not just routine questions. They feel pointed, like they’re trying to connect me to something improper, like I’m crooked or cutting corners.

My supervisor keeps telling me it’s just normal review, but I know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated. Like people are trying to build a case, or at least make me look unreliable so the award doesn’t mean anything. I get that someone on the outside might say, “Oh, that’s just office politics,” or “You’re reading into it,” but when you’re in it and you see the pattern, it’s hard to ignore.
Have you had similar concerns about people plotting against you or twisting your words in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Not really outside of work, no. I mean, I’m not saying every person everywhere is doing something. It’s specifically tied to my job, to the reports, to the budget questions, and honestly to what changed after I got that county safety award.

That’s the part people keep missing. Before that, my reports were fine, or if there was a question, it was normal—clarify this, adjust that wording, whatever. But after the award, certain people started treating my work differently, like they were looking for a way to make it seem like I’d done something wrong. They take wording from my inspection reports and twist it, like they’re trying to make it sound like I meant something I didn’t. Then the budget questions come in, and they’re asked in this pointed way, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or careless.

So no, I don’t go around thinking neighbors or strangers are plotting against me. It’s not like that. It’s this coordinated thing at work, and my supervisor keeps calling it normal review, but I know what normal review feels like. This feels like they’re trying to discredit me.
Do you feel certain that your coworkers are deliberately misrepresenting your work and trying to discredit you, even though there may not be clear proof of this?

Yes, I do feel certain. I know that sounds like a strong word, and I understand you’re asking because there isn’t some document in my hand that says, “We are trying to discredit him.” But when you’re the one going through it, and you see the same pattern over and over, it stops feeling like coincidence.

Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been acting like my inspection reports are suspicious somehow. They’ll take a sentence or a phrase and twist it around, like I meant something I didn’t mean, or like I left something out on purpose. And then the budget questions come up in this pointed way, not like normal review, but like they’re trying to make me look crooked or careless.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just routine, that reports get reviewed and questions get asked, and I know that. I’ve done this job long enough to know what normal review looks like. This isn’t that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to chip away at my reputation so the award doesn’t mean anything, or so people start doubting whether I deserved it. So yes, even if I can’t prove every piece of it on paper, I can tell what’s happening.

Do you feel completely certain that your coworkers are misrepresenting your work, to the point where no explanation or reassurance from others, including your supervisor, could change your mind about it?

Yes. I mean… I don’t want to sound like I’m being unreasonable, but yes, I feel sure about it.

That’s the whole reason I came here, because ever since that county safety award, the way certain people at work have been handling my inspection reports has changed. They’ll pull out wording and act like I meant something improper, or they’ll make it sound like I was trying to hide something when I wasn’t. And then the budget questions come up in this very pointed way, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or careless. It’s not the same as normal review. I know what normal review is.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s routine, that everyone’s reports get checked, that questions are just questions. But that doesn’t explain the pattern. It doesn’t explain why it started after the award, or why the questions feel like they’re aimed at my reputation, not the actual work.

So, could reassurance change my mind? Not really, no. Not just someone telling me, “Don’t worry about it.” Because I’m the one seeing how they’re twisting things. I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
How long have you felt certain that your coworkers have been deliberately misrepresenting your work and trying to discredit you?

It’s been about a year now. I’d say it started right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative, or at least that’s when I really noticed the shift.

Before that, I wasn’t thinking this way. I wasn’t watching every comment on my reports or wondering why budget questions were being asked a certain way. But after that award, it was like the tone changed. Not all at once in one dramatic moment, but little by little—questions that felt pointed, wording from my reports getting picked apart, people acting like there was something suspicious where there wasn’t.

So, yeah, about a year. And it’s been consistent enough over that time that I don’t see it as just a misunderstanding anymore.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that were completely different from those around you, such as thinking you had special powers, a unique mission, or that you were being sent secret messages?

No, not like special powers or some unique mission or secret messages, if that’s what you mean. I don’t think I’m being sent codes or anything like that.

What I’m talking about is very specific to work. I’m here because ever since that county safety award, certain people at work started handling my inspection reports differently. They’ll twist wording, take things out of context, and then these budget questions come up in this pointed way, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or careless. And when my supervisor says it’s just normal review, I hear that, but I know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.

So it’s not that I think I have some special role or power. It’s that I can tell what’s happening with my work and my reputation.
Can you think of any time when someone tried to reassure you that your work was being reviewed normally, and you considered that they might be right?

I mean… I’ve tried to consider it, yes, because my supervisor has said that more than once. He’ll say, “This is just standard review,” or “These questions come up for everybody,” and I don’t want to be the kind of person who just dismisses everything out of hand.

So in the moment, I’ll sit there and think, okay, maybe I’m being too sensitive about the wording, maybe it’s just because I care about the reports and I know what I meant when I wrote them. But then the same thing happens again. Certain lines from my inspection reports get pulled out like they’re trying to make them sound improper, and then these budget questions come up in this pointed way, like the implication is I did something careless or crooked. And it’s always framed like, “We’re just asking,” but it doesn’t feel like just asking.

So, yes, I’ve considered what my supervisor said, but I don’t really believe it. Not after the pattern I’ve seen since that county safety award. Normal review doesn’t feel like people twisting your work to damage your reputation. That’s the part I can’t ignore.
Has there been any time when you saw direct evidence that your coworkers were not misrepresenting your work, or when reassurance from others made you question your belief at all?

I’ve looked for that, honestly. I’m not trying to be unreasonable about it. There have been times where my supervisor sat me down and said, “No, this is just normal review,” or “Nobody is accusing you of anything,” and I tried to take that in. I really did.

But I can’t say it changed my mind much, because the same pattern keeps showing up. Ever since that county safety award, certain people at work have been handling my inspection reports differently. They’ll pull out wording like it means something it doesn’t, or they’ll ask these budget questions in this pointed way, like they’re trying to make it look like I’m careless or crooked. And maybe one time, sure, you could say it was routine. Maybe even twice. But when it keeps happening with the same kind of tone and the same implications, it’s hard for me to accept that it’s innocent.

So, no, I haven’t really seen direct evidence that they’re not misrepresenting my work. I’ve heard reassurance, but it feels more like people trying to smooth it over than actually explain why my reports are being twisted. I know what normal review looks like, and this doesn’t feel like that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me while still being able to say, “We were just asking questions.”
Have you ever seen any direct evidence that your coworkers were not trying to misrepresent your work, or that your reports were being reviewed in a standard way?

No, not really. I mean, I’ve heard people say it’s standard, especially my supervisor. He’ll say, “This is just how reports get reviewed,” or “Nobody’s trying to make you look bad,” and I understand what he’s saying. I’m not ignoring that.

But direct evidence? No. What I’ve seen is the opposite. Since that county safety award, certain people have been taking my inspection reports and twisting the wording, pulling out lines like they mean something shady when that’s not what I wrote. Then the budget questions come up in this very pointed way, like they’re trying to imply I did something careless or crooked without actually saying it outright.

And that’s the thing that bothers me. If it was just normal review, it wouldn’t keep feeling like the same kind of setup over and over. I know what normal review looks like. I’ve had my reports checked before. This feels different. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me but keep it just vague enough that they can say, “We’re only asking questions.” So no, I haven’t seen anything that convinces me they’re not doing that.

Even when people have shown you that your reports were reviewed the same way as others’ or explained that the questions were routine, have you still felt absolutely certain that they were trying to discredit you?

Yes. I mean… I know how that sounds when you say “absolutely certain,” because people act like certainty means I’m not listening. But I have listened. My supervisor has explained it more than once, and he’ll show me that other reports get reviewed too, that budget questions come up as part of the process. I understand that on paper.

But it still doesn’t change what I can tell is happening with mine. Since that county safety award, certain people have been picking apart my inspection reports in a way that feels different. They don’t just ask normal clarification questions. They pull out certain lines, they put this tone on it, and then the budget questions come in like they’re hinting I did something careless or crooked. They don’t have to say it directly for me to know what they’re doing.

So, yes, even when someone says, “Look, this is routine,” I still believe there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me. Maybe they can make it look normal from the outside, but from where I’m sitting, with the pattern and the timing and the way they keep framing things, it’s not normal review. It’s them trying to damage my reputation while keeping it just vague enough to deny.
